Epoch 4 carries two changes. The queue half is bookkeeping and cannot move a verdict: a row the publisher withheld, or one whose instrument failure has exhausted its retries, is now settled at the harness hash that refused it instead of being handed back to every later slice. The DRIVER half can and does. measure-macos.sh held an absolute npm path captured before any era pin existed, so its unjailed control ran the era Node with the harness npm's JavaScript and recorded a package verdict for a failure that was ours. And all three drivers' npm reference arm -- the arm that decides whether a nub failure is BROKEN-UNJAILED-NUB or BROKEN-WITHOUT-JAIL-TOO -- ran undated on the harness toolchain, so a spurious npm failure exonerated nub and filed a candidate nub defect as a dead package. Only those two verdicts are reachable by either bug: both act on the unjailed control, and a record that got past it ran npm correctly. Every MINIMUM measurement therefore stands.

Epoch 5 dates the SCAFFOLD install in all three drivers. The package fetch has carried --before since F2 and the npm reference arm got it in epoch 4, but the second install -- the one that supplies the binaries a lifecycle script names -- never did, so it pulled TODAY's build tools into a tree pinned to the package's own era and the era Node could not parse them. observe-only.mjs:330 already records this exact failure and its fix; neither driver received it. THE FIX STANDS ON THAT MECHANISM ALONE. It was originally justified here by a ratio -- 178 of 282 BROKEN-WITHOUT-JAIL-TOO records carrying 'Error: Unexpected token' -- and that ratio is RETRACTED: 178 counted OCCURRENCES across every retained log while 282 counted verdict LINES, two different denominators reported as one fraction. Counted per RECORD over the 286 retained darwin logs, 'Unexpected token' appears in 16 of 128 BROKEN-WITHOUT-JAIL-TOO records (12.5%) and in 70 of 140 MINIMUM records (50%) -- four times more common where the measurement SUCCEEDED, so it is non-fatal noise and not this bug's signature. Only 6 of the first 53 epoch-5 darwin records ran a scaffold at all, so this scope is wider than the change warrants; it is left as issued rather than churned a third time on a corpus that has already absorbed two policy changes. Same scope as epoch 4 and for the same reason: the scaffold runs before the unjailed control, so only a record that failed that control can have been affected, and every MINIMUM measurement stands.

Epoch 6 closes the two doors through which a second runner could drain beside a live one. The workflow header has carried a RUN ONE RUNNER AT A TIME block, and the measurement behind it, since 2026-08-23 -- two overlapping runners give `completed 0 row(s)`, because every runner rewrites the WHOLE queue and the second write is built on a pre-claim snapshot -- but nothing enforced it. Door one: `push: branches: [probe/corpus-v2-lane]` carries no paths filter, so any human or agent commit to the drain branch dispatches a full drain; the runner's own record pushes are exempt only because GitHub raises no workflow event for a GITHUB_TOKEN push, which is an accident rather than a design. MEASURED 2026-08-28: a one-file commit to invalidation.json dispatched run 33139321538, whose "Claim a slice" step reached success and took 10 rows before it was cancelled by hand; the live darwin slice was unharmed only because it had already finished. Door two: two workflow_dispatch runs, which no trigger gate can catch. The fix gates a push drain behind a [drain] marker in the head commit message and adds a preflight that refuses to claim while an OLDER run of this workflow is alive. THIS INVALIDATES NOTHING, AND THE EMPTY SCOPE SAYS SO EXACTLY. Neither change touches a driver, an arm, a toolchain or a verdict; both act on whether a run claims at all. A record measured at epoch 5 is the same record it would be at epoch 6.

So writing about the gate in a commit message opts that push in -- MEASURED by epoch 6's own commit, whose body explained the feature, spelled the token out while doing so, and dispatched run 33139919598. Nothing was harmed: the preflight found no older runner and let it through, which is the right answer. The epoch-6 version said the accidental run and the live darwin slice "never overlapped at the queue", and that a push needs ten-odd minutes to reach the claim step. Epoch 10 adds one test file. The workflow header asserts that two concurrent runners erase each other's queue claims, because every runner rewrites the whole queue from a pre-claim snapshot. That is a real failure mode for a last-write-wins push, and this lane does not have one: the claim step re-claims against the new head when its push is rejected. claim-cas.test.mjs pins that by driving the step's OWN shell, extracted from the workflow rather than paraphrased, against two clones of a scratch repo where the second is cloned BEFORE the first claims. Both runners' claims survive on origin and the slices are disjoint; a last-write-wins control force-pushes the stale snapshot and DOES erase, so the green is not vacuous. It covers the CLAIM path only and does not make parallel draining safe. THIS INVALIDATES NOTHING: a new test file, no driver or arm touched.

Epoch 11 extends claim-cas.test.mjs from the claim push to the full cycle: two runners claim, publish INTERLEAVED, and complete, and origin must end up holding every record and every closed row from both. It passes on current code. Disabling the publisher's queue refresh makes it reproduce the header's failure exactly -- rows whose record published never closed -- so the test detects the real thing rather than passing vacuously. But that line has been in the publisher since its first commit on 2026-08-06, seventeen days BEFORE the 2026-08-23 two-runner measurement, so it was never the fix and the observation stays unexplained. The drain remains serial. THIS INVALIDATES NOTHING: one test file.

Epoch 12 fixes the end-of-slice commit guard, which failed a slice that had fully SUCCEEDED. The publisher pushes each record as it is measured and its --reconcile closes the row as it lands, so a slice can reach the commit step with every record already on the branch and every row already done -- nothing left to stage. The old guard read "manifest non-empty AND nothing staged" as a failed sparse add and exited 1, which failed the job, skipped the queue-status and chaining steps, and discarded the --complete bookkeeping so settled rows were never recorded and the re-measure loop returned. The line written for this case, "already up to date -- records already landed", was UNREACHABLE: the guard fires first whenever the manifest is non-empty, i.e. whenever anything published. The discriminator is now whether the manifest's records are ON the branch, not whether anything was staged; a record absent from HEAD still FATALs, and names itself. THIS INVALIDATES NOTHING. The branch is only reachable when nothing was staged, so no record and no queue content changes -- only the job's exit status. No arm, driver or verdict is touched.

Epoch 13 gives the era Python to the nub arms. Until now only the OBSERVE arm and the npm reference arm held it: the VERIFY ladder and the jail-off control fell back to the runner's ambient Python, so node-gyp inside them ran a different interpreter from the arm they are compared against. MEASURED on node-sass@9.0.0 (darwin, era Node 18.20.8, epoch 5, driver.out retained beside the record): every nub arm died on ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'distutils' -- Python 3.12 removed it and node-gyp 8.4.1 needs it -- while era-python.mjs --era 18 returns Python 3.9, which has it. npm, holding that 3.9, installed the package cleanly, so the control reported "npm installs this package but nub cannot" and the record was filed BROKEN-UNJAILED-NUB: a claimed NUB INSTALL DEFECT manufactured entirely by the harness. This is the epoch-4 npm-reference bug on the Python axis and it points the other way -- there a spurious failure exonerated nub, here it convicts it. On macOS sudo resets the environment, so PYTHON now rides the same env vector as PATH in asIdentity rather than relying on an exported value. SCOPE: every verdict a wrong interpreter can reach. A Python failure is GRANT-INDEPENDENT -- it fails identically at every rung -- so it cannot produce a spuriously WIDE minimum; it produces total failure, which lands in one of the six verdicts named here. A record that found a working grant had a working Python, so every MINIMUM stands. RESIDUAL RISK, stated rather than hidden: a package whose ambient Python worked may resolve node-gyp paths differently under the era Python, which could in principle shift a minimum grant. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE is already set on every arm, which removes the obvious such path. Cost measured before landing: 226 of 1906 reusable records (11.9%), leaving 1680.

Epoch 14 makes every driver print WHY the unjailed era fetch failed. All three captured npm's diagnosis already -- the shell drivers into "$OBS/fetch.log", the windows driver into a string -- and all three then discarded it, so the record kept only the verdict. MEASURED corpus-wide 2026-08-28: 165 of the 1409 BROKEN-WITHOUT-JAIL-TOO records exit at that fetch, and every one of the 165 has a driver.out of roughly eighteen lines carrying no reason at all (@ffmpeg-installer/linux-ia32@4.1.0 on darwin-arm64 is a worked example: it stops one line after ERA-RESOLUTION). That is exactly the bucket this corpus exists to split -- a package genuinely gone from the registry and a dated fetch asking for something that never existed produce byte-identical records, so no amount of re-measuring can separate a dead package from a harness defect. Each driver now prints a bounded 20-line tail, the idiom npm_ok already used on its own fetch. The darwin driver additionally captures the rc on its own line, because the exit now interpolates it and an unbound name under `set -u` aborts the whole run -- a runtime failure `bash -n` does not catch. The windows tail is deliberately one line and sits AFTER emitBinaryProvenance(), since venue-provenance-on-exit.test.mjs scans only five lines past the verdict for that call. Zero records are invalidated: the change adds output and changes no verdict any record could have reached.

Epoch 15 gives the LINUX jail-off control the era PATH, so the two arms that decide fault finally hold the same toolchain. measure.sh never modifies its own PATH -- ERA_PATH is a SEPARATE variable (ERA_PATH="$ERA_NODE_BIN:$PATH") -- so every arm opts in locally: the scaffold, OBSERVE, each verify rung and npm_ok's two installs all set it, and unjailed_nub_ok set nothing. Its lifecycle scripts therefore ran node/node-gyp from the RUNNER's Node while npm_ok, the arm it is compared against, ran the package's era Node -- and when that difference makes nub fail where npm succeeds, the record is filed BROKEN-UNJAILED-NUB: a nub install defect manufactured by the harness. Same class as the epoch-4 npm-reference fix and the epoch-13 Python fix, and specifically the half of epoch 13 left undone -- that change set PYTHON on the child env and left PATH behind, giving this arm the era interpreter under the runner's Node, a combination no real install ever has. Passing --spawn-path from the driver is NOT sufficient on its own: asIdentity returns [cmd, args] unchanged when there is no sudo user, so on Linux the flag was accepted and ignored, and the child env is what carries it. DARWIN IS UNAFFECTED -- sudo resets the environment, which forced it to pass PATH explicitly from the start; its protection was a side effect of the spawn strategy rather than a decision, which is why Linux never received it. WIN32 IS NOT FIXED and is stated rather than hidden: measure-windows.mjs runs its control in-process from imported classify/offSwitchEngaged and never calls this module, so the change does not reach it; win32 holds 5 valid records and is outside the current drain. SCOPE: the control only runs after every verify rung has already failed, so it cannot reach MINIMUM -- a record that found a working grant never consulted it -- and the three verdicts named here are the ones classify() can return. Cost measured before landing: 0 of 1680 reusable records, because epoch 13 already invalidated those same verdicts and no slice has yet measured at epoch 13 or later. This epoch also makes the control PRINT what nub said before accusing it. The arm's output was captured into logs and written by writeLogs into a scratch dir that is discarded, so a real nub defect and a harness asymmetry left byte-identical records. MEASURED on linux-x64 @stdlib/math-base-special-signum@0.0.6: the record carries the full node-gyp failure for every verify rung and not one line about why the control failed -- and both arms resolved the IDENTICAL tree there (digest 8189fa7ae585, 74 specs each), which is what isolates the difference to execution rather than resolution. That is the epoch-14 blind spot one arm over, on the arm where attribution matters most.

Epoch 16 settles a withheld row at the hash the slice MEASURED under, not the hash on disk when --complete runs. settledAtHash carries one promise, stated in claim-slice.mjs itself -- the attempt happened at THIS instrument -- and the claim path reopens the row the moment the harness moves off that hash. That is the difference between settled and abandoned. The end-of-slice commit step broke the promise by construction: git reset --hard origin/$BRANCH pulls harness/ forward to whatever landed on the branch WHILE the slice was measuring, AND restores queue-v2.ndjson from origin, discarding the correct settle the Collect verdicts step already wrote so the rows are claimed again and --complete re-runs from the reset tree. MEASURED on run 33167330698: it measured at epoch 12, three harness epochs landed while it ran, and it settled 16 withheld rows at the EPOCH-15 digest -- frozen against an epoch-15 attempt that never happened, and specifically against the era-toolchain fixes in epochs 13/14/15 that are the likeliest thing to resolve why they regressed. Harness fixes landing mid-drain is DESIGNED here, so this is the normal case rather than a rare race. The runner now captures the identity before the reset loop and passes --measured-harness-sha. Landing this epoch also REMEDIATES the 16 rows for free: their settledAtHash no longer equals the current instrument, so the claim path reopens them, which is exactly the mechanism the hash scoping was designed for. Zero records invalidated -- no verdict can change.

Their chained successors 33196045838 and 33201592660 reported "instrument: epoch 3 b21a24cef3e3ab8c" and "find: records-v2: No such file or directory", claimed 60 rows each off main's queue, and died. The head_branch field on each run is an INPUT to the run rather than something the run writes, so the correlation is not the emit-ordering artifact that killed the era-pin finding. THE ALTERNATING PASS/FAIL WAS READ FOR TWO SLICES AS AN INTERMITTENT FALSIFICATION-GATE FLAKE, AND IT WAS NOTHING OF THE KIND. The gate refused to measure with a harness thirteen epochs behind the nub binary it was handed, which is precisely its job, and that refusal is the only reason no epoch-3 measurement ever entered a corpus. The residue is 120 claimed-and-stranded rows on main's own queue-v2.ndjson, a file this lane does not read, which --reclaim-stale owns whenever anyone runs that lane. MEASUREMENT-NEUTRAL, hence the empty verdict list. The change decides which REF a successor run checks out; it cannot alter what any arm of any driver observes about any package. The v1 runner corpus-queue-runner.yml carried the identical defect and is fixed in the same commit -- it is not an instrument input, so it moves no digest. chain-stays-on-branch.test.mjs guards the CLASS rather than the site: every non-comment `gh workflow run` in the workflow tree must name a --ref, and any dispatch passing chain=true must ride $GITHUB_REF_NAME rather than a literal branch. Both halves were driven red before landing, and a known-answer control asserts the scanner still finds both runners -- without it every assertion passes vacuously the moment the scanner breaks. Epoch 17 carries a second, independent fix to the same slice-losing class. claim-cas.test.mjs tore its scratch root down while a DETACHED git gc was still writing into the bare origin: receive-pack runs gc --auto after every push it accepts and gc.autoDetach defaults to true, so the gc outlives the synchronous push the fixture blocks on. MEASURED 2026-08-28 on run 33202504594, dispatched correctly on probe/corpus-v2-lane at epoch 16: the last-write-wins control asserted correctly and then died in teardown with ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir /tmp/claimcas-ClEEqA/origin.git, which failed the whole harness-suite step and cost the slice -- the job never reached Claim a slice, so nothing was claimed and nothing was stranded. Fixed at the source by disabling receive.autogc, gc.auto and gc.autoDetach on the fixture origin; the teardown additionally routes through a documented discard() helper carrying Node fs.rm maxRetries, which guards no assertion and cannot turn a red test green. The contention control still passes, so the fixture still reproduces the failure mode it exists to demonstrate. Also measurement-neutral: it touches a test fixture only, and no driver arm reads it.

Epoch 18 makes a drained lane hand the chain off instead of ending the whole drain.

THE DEFECT. The chaining runner dispatches its successor with the SAME `os` it ran, and its
claim loop sets DRAINED=1 as soon as its own lane claims nothing. The dispatch step was gated
on `env.DRAINED != '1'`, so the FIRST lane to empty stopped the corpus for every lane -- and it
stopped it silently, because a drained lane exits 0 and looks exactly like a successful slice.

MEASURED 2026-08-29 on the live queue at HEAD 352933e8e: linux 850 pending / 60 claimed, macos
1652 pending, windows 2265 pending. At the observed rate (~45 records per ~66-minute slice, and
per-slice overhead measured at 1.3 of 66.2 minutes, so the rate is real work not setup) linux
would have emptied in roughly 19 slices -- about 21 hours -- and halted the drain near 41%
coverage with 3917 rows never measured and nothing reporting that anything had stopped.

THE FIX. `claim-slice.mjs --next-os <ordered,lanes>` prints the first listed lane that still
holds PENDING rows, or nothing when they are all empty. The drained branch computes it into
NEXT_OS, and the dispatch fires when a successor exists, targeting `${NEXT_OS:-$OS_NAME}` so
the ordinary hop is byte-for-byte unchanged and there is no second dispatch site to drift.
A fully drained corpus still ends the chain -- that is the one honest place to stop. `claimed`
deliberately does not count as pending, so a row another runner is mid-measure on cannot
resurrect a chain.

A BUG THIS CHANGE INTRODUCED AND THE SUITE CAUGHT. The first application put the explanatory
comment BETWEEN the `--ref` continuation and the `-f os=` line. Bash folds a backslash
continuation before honouring `#`, so the comment swallowed the rest of the gh invocation and
`-f os=...` became its own command -- a runtime failure, not a syntax error, which is why
`bash -n` reported the file clean. It is now verified by EXECUTING the extracted command
against a gh stub in both modes: NEXT_OS unset dispatches os=linux, NEXT_OS=macos dispatches
os=macos, one call each. `bash -n` is not a sufficient instrument for this class.

REFUTATION FIRST, because it redirects the work: a denial witness scored on the VERIFY arm cannot rescue the gate-vacuous narrowings, and building a win32 capture for that purpose would have been wasted. Such a witness answers "did the script attempt a refused access inside the dropped scope?", and CLEAN means it never asked. The twelve records are precisely the population where the script never asked because it never DID anything, so CLEAN is guaranteed by construction and licensing on it publishes the under-grant. The detector cannot separate "needs nothing" from "did nothing".

THE MECHANISM, read out of the real tarballs rather than inferred. Ten of the twelve are the whole @pulumi family plus backport, and their OBSERVE writes block is EMPTY -- zero writes in any bucket. @pulumi/gcp scripts/install-pulumi-plugin.js spawns `pulumi plugin install`, and when the Pulumi CLI is absent the spawn returns ENOENT, the script prints to stderr and then calls process.exit(0) UNCONDITIONALLY. On a runner without that binary the package therefore writes nothing, opens nothing and exits 0, and the harness synthesizes the empty grant. On a machine that HAS the CLI the same script downloads plugins into ~/.pulumi/plugins over the network -- write.userHome plus network, exactly the grant these records would have dropped. The same family, the same script, opposite measurements, decided by an unrelated binary being on PATH.

It is evaluated BEFORE the evidence rules, so no present or future licence can outrank it. Base-covered buckets count as effect, or @azure-devops/mcp scores idle; execs deliberately do not, because an ENOENT spawnSync is an ATTEMPTED exec and counting it scores the whole @pulumi family as having worked. It invalidates nothing on its own -- the existing rule already withholds these twelve; the veto changes the REASON for ten of them, from "no descent arm went red", which points at building a red arm that cannot exist, to naming the no-effect state.
